title_en: 271: David Rubenstein, Co-Founder of The Carlyle Group, on the Business of Sports, Investi
title_zh: 271: David Rubenstein（The Carlyle Group 联合创始人）谈体育生意与投资
subtitle_zh: 从收购 Orioles 到对话多位体育老板，揭示体育投资的商业逻辑与领导力教训
description: 271: David Rubenstein, Co-Founder of The Carlyle Group, on the Business of Sports, Investi

turns.en: Sports teams have become some of the world's most valuable assets. Over the past two decades, franchise values have soared, institutional investors have entered the market, and ownership has evolved from a passion project into a sophisticated business.
turns.zh: 体育球队已经成为全球最有价值的资产之一。过去二十年里，球队估值飙升，机构投资者纷纷入场，所有权也从一腔热爱的爱好变成了一门精密的生意。

turns.en: But owning a team isn't like owning any other company. The product is emotional. This isn't measured just in profits, but in championships, civic pride, and the connection between a city and its fans.
turns.zh: 但拥有一支球队和拥有一家普通公司完全不同。它的产品关乎情感——衡量的标准不仅是利润，还有冠军头衔、城市的自豪感，以及一座城市与它的球迷之间的情感纽带。

turns.en: Welcome to The Bid, where we break down what's happening in the markets and explore the forces changing the economy and finance. I'm Oscar Polito.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 The Bid，在这个节目里我们拆解市场动态，探索正在改变经济和金融的力量。我是 Oscar Pulido。

turns.en: Today's guest has spent decades thinking about long-term investing and value creation. David Rubenstein is the co-founder and co-chairman of the Carlisle Group, one of the world's largest private equity investment firms.
turns.zh: 今天的嘉宾几十年来一直在思考长期投资和价值创造。David Rubenstein 是 The Carlyle Group 的联合创始人兼联席主席，这是全球最大的私募股权投资（private equity）机构之一。

turns.en: Over the course of his career, these helped shape the modern private equity industry, interviewed presidents, CEOs, and global leaders, and become one of the most recognized voices on leadership and investing.
turns.zh: 在他的职业生涯中，他帮助塑造了现代私募股权行业，采访了各国总统、CEO 和全球领袖，成为领导力和投资领域最具辨识度的声音之一。

turns.en: More recently, he took on a very different role, leading the ownership group that purchased his hometown Baltimore Orioles. His latest book, Inside the Owners Box, draws on that experience, as well as conversations with some of the most successful owners in sports.
turns.zh: 最近，他担任了一个非常不同的角色——带领投资财团收购了他的家乡球队 Baltimore Orioles。他的新书 Inside the Owner's Box 正是基于这段经历，也融合了他与体育界最成功的一些老板们的对话。

turns.en: To explore what sports ownership can teach us about leadership, investing, and building institutions that last. David, thank you so much for joining us on The Bid.
turns.zh: 我们一起探讨体育所有权能教会我们关于领导力、投资和打造长青机构的智慧。David，非常感谢你来到 The Bid。

turns.en: My pleasure. Thank you very much for having me. Well, David, when people hear your name, I think it's fair to say they think of the Carlisle Group, they think about the private equity industry that you have helped create.
turns.zh: 我的荣幸，谢谢你邀请我。嗯，David，一提到你的名字，大家想到的肯定是 The Carlyle Group，想到的是你参与创建的私募股权行业。

turns.en: Most people don't realize that you're also a owner of a sports franchise, and that's really the topic of conversation that we want to have here today, which is about investing in the sports industry.
turns.zh: 大多数人并不知道你还是一个体育球队的老板，而这正是我们今天想聊的话题——体育行业的投资。

turns.en: So I want to ask you, when you went about buying a sports team, how did you consider this as an investment opportunity? Were you looking at it as an entertainment business, a media business, or something entirely different?
turns.zh: 所以我想问你，当初你去买一支球队的时候，你怎么把它当作一个投资机会来看待的？你把它看作是一个娱乐生意、一个媒体生意，还是完全不同的东西？

turns.en: Well, I did it for a reason that's unrelated to investment. I'm from Baltimore. I felt over the years I've been financially successful. I've given away a great deal of money.
turns.zh: 嗯，我做这件事的原因跟投资无关。我来自 Baltimore。这些年我在财务上算是比较成功的，也捐出了大量的钱。

turns.en: I was an original signer of the Giving Pledge, and I've tried to give away enormous amounts of my net worth, but most of that has probably been the universities my family has been associated with or to the Washington, D.C. area where I've lived for the last 40, some years.
turns.zh: 我是 Giving Pledge 最早的一批签署者之一，我一直试图捐出我净资产的很大一部分，但大多数可能都给了我家族关联的大学，或者给了华盛顿特区——我在那里生活了几十年。

turns.en: I really didn't do as much for Baltimore as I thought I should. I grew up there, and my parents grew up there, and my parents are married there.
turns.zh: 我确实没有为 Baltimore 做那么多我觉得应该做的事。我在那里长大，我父母也在那里长大，他们在那里结的婚。

turns.en: They raised me there. They're buried there. I'm going to be buried there. I thought, what have I really done from Baltimore? I've been involved in Johns Hopkins and been on their boards, but I hadn't given staggering sums there.
turns.zh: 他们在那里把我养大。他们葬在那里。我以后也会葬在那里。我就想，我到底为 Baltimore 做了什么？我参与过 Johns Hopkins 的事务，也在那边的董事会待过，但没有捐过什么特别大的数目。

turns.en: So, I viewed it more as a philanthropic gesture. I didn't want to lose money, but I viewed it as a way to give back to Baltimore for the good fortune I've had from coming from Baltimore.
turns.zh: 所以我把它更多地看作一个公益行为。我不想亏钱，但我把它当作一种回报 Baltimore 的方式，感谢我从 Baltimore 走出来所获得的幸运。

turns.en: And you mentioned Baltimore, and in fact, the sports team that you are the owner of are the Baltimore Orioles, which is a major league baseball team.
turns.zh: 你提到了 Baltimore，实际上你拥有的那支球队是 Baltimore Orioles，是一支美国职业棒球大联盟球队。

turns.en: You made that investment back in 2024, and as mentioned, most people know you're from the private equity industry, so they know that you know how to evaluate an investment.
turns.zh: 你在 2024 年做了这笔投资，正如前面提到的，大多数人知道你是做私募股权出身的，所以大家都知道你懂得怎么评估一项投资。

turns.en: But what made this opportunity different from every other investment you've ever considered? On the private equity road, you're trying to make money, and you're always looking at certain rates of return.
turns.zh: 但这个机会有什么特别之处，跟你之前考虑过的所有投资都不一样？在私募股权这条路上，你做的就是赚钱，你一直在看的是特定的回报率。

turns.en: You know your investors are looking for double-digit rates of return and so forth. In this particular case, I didn't really focus on that quite the same way.
turns.zh: 你知道你的投资人要的是两位数回报率等等。但在这个具体的案例里，我没有完全那样去关注。

turns.en: I didn't want to lose money, as I mentioned, but I really viewed it as a civic gesture, and therefore I wanted people to come along with me who were involved in helping Baltimore grow to be a more significant city, helping Baltimore to be revitalized, and they might like baseball too, and so the combination of factors.
turns.zh: 正如我说的，我不想亏钱，但我真的把它看作是一种城市公益行为。所以我想跟我一起参与的人，是那些在帮助 Baltimore 发展成一个更重要的城市的人，帮助 Baltimore 重新振兴的人，他们可能也喜欢棒球，所以是这些因素的结合。

turns.en: Now the world has changed, and it was the case many years ago that people made sports investments because they really loved the sports. There's no doubt today that a lot of people are attracted to it because the profitability seems to be pretty high if you get lucky and you get at the right time.
turns.zh: 但世界已经变了。很多年前人们投资体育确实是因为他们真的热爱这项运动。但今天毫无疑问，很多人被吸引进来是因为如果你运气好、在恰当的时机入场，利润率看起来相当可观。

turns.en: When you talk about the civic gesture, maybe say a little bit more about that. I'm familiar with the Baltimore Orioles, and I know Camden Yard sits right in Baltimore Harbor.
turns.zh: 你提到城市公益，能不能多讲一点？我对 Baltimore Orioles 比较熟悉，我知道 Camden Yards 就在 Baltimore 港口边上。

turns.en: It's central to the community of Baltimore, but talk a little bit more about the importance that sports teams have to their local cities. When I grew up in Baltimore, it was the ninth biggest city in the United States in the 1950s and 60s.
turns.zh: 它对 Baltimore 社区来说是核心，但你再多讲讲球队对所在城市的重要性吧。我在 Baltimore 长大的时候，它在五六十年代还是美国第九大城市。

turns.en: Now it's not even the top 20 in terms of population. It's lost enormous population, had a lot of crime issues, a lot of drug-related issues, a lot of problems in the city, and they've lost their corporate headquarters more or less, a very few large corporate headquarters.
turns.zh: 现在按人口排连前 20 都进不了了。人口流失了巨大的规模，犯罪问题很严重，毒品问题也很多，城市面临各种困境，企业总部也基本上搬走了，大型企业总部已经所剩无几。

turns.en: The city's tax base is going way down, and therefore the city doesn't have the kind of resources that other cities might have. I should point out that in the entire United States, there are only two cities in the country that are not in a county.
turns.zh: 城市的税基大幅下滑，所以它没有像其他城市那样的财政资源。我要指出的是，在整个美国，只有两个城市是不属于任何县的。

turns.en: One is Baltimore and one is St. Louis, which means when you move out of Baltimore City or St. Louis, none of the tax revenues that you might give to a surrounding county go back to the city.
turns.zh: 一个是 Baltimore，一个是 St. Louis。也就是说，当你从 Baltimore 市或 St. Louis 搬出去之后，你交给周边县的税款不会回流给城市本身。

turns.en: In this particular case, I thought that Baltimore could be revitalized a bit if I bought the team and put more money into it and helped the city.
turns.zh: 在这个具体的情况下，我觉得如果我买下球队、往里投入更多资金、帮助这座城市，Baltimore 也许能重新振兴起来。

turns.en: In that way, we try to revitalize the downtown area where the stadium is built. The stadium is called Camden Yards, and when it opened in the early 90s, it was revolutionary for baseball because it was a downtown stadium arena, which hadn't been built that way in recent years.
turns.zh: 所以我们在努力振兴球场所在的市中心区域。球场叫 Camden Yards，它在九十年代初启用的时候，对棒球界来说是革命性的，因为它是一座建在市中心的球场，而那种方式已经很多年没有新建筑了。

turns.en: In recent years, you built things in the suburbs, and this one was designed to look like an old park, Wrigley Field or Fenway Park, and capture the imagination of fans.
turns.zh: 之前那些年都在郊区建球场，而 Camden Yards 被设计成老式球场的样子——像 Wrigley Field 或 Fenway Park 那样——重新抓住了球迷的想象力。

turns.en: Enormous number of people came out to the games, but also people who began building stadiums from 1991 on all wanted to have a model like Camden Yards.
turns.zh: 大量观众涌向比赛，而且从 1991 年开始建新球场的城市都想以 Camden Yards 为样板。

turns.en: Even if people don't follow baseball or not familiar with it, globally, sports are very relevant. I think people can relate to the fact of going to an arena or a stadium, a site that is the home of their sports team.
turns.zh: 即使人们不关注棒球、对它不熟悉，体育运动在全球都非常有意义。我觉得人们能体会到那种去体育馆或球场、去到他们主队所在之处的感觉。

turns.en: As you mentioned, Camden Yards has been around since the early 90s. I must profess that having been there recently, we were talking about that a little bit beforehand, and it looks like what I remember when I went for the first time 20 or 25 years ago.
turns.zh: 正如你提到的，Camden Yards 从九十年代初就有了。我必须承认，我最近去过那里——我们之前也聊到这个——它看起来跟我二十或二十五年前第一次去时记忆中的样子一模一样。

turns.en: It seems like you've already been making some investments there. Well, the state of Maryland actually owns Camden Yards, a Maryland stadium authority, and they gave us money to refurbish it, and we've done a bigger scoreboard, better sound system, better dugouts in play and clubhouses, more restaurant-related facilities, better food facilities, and many different things, and we've made it a better experience.
turns.zh: 看起来你们已经在球场上做了一些投入。嗯，实际上马里兰州政府拥有 Camden Yards，是马里兰州的体育场管理局，他们拨了钱让我们翻新。我们换了更大的记分屏、更好的音响系统、更好的球员休息区和更衣室、更多的餐饮设施、更好的食品选择，还有很多其他改进，让整体体验变得更好了。

turns.en: Remember, in baseball, what you're doing in all sports, you're trying to get people to come to the stadium, and you want them to have a pleasurable experience.
turns.zh: 你要记住，在棒球里——其实在所有体育项目里——你要做的是让人们来到球场，你要让他们有一个愉快的体验。

turns.en: So you want to have a good winning team, which will always bring fans to the stadium, but you want to have the food be good, the amenities be good, the whole experience be something that they think is worth the price that they pay.
turns.zh: 所以你需要一支有竞争力的球队，好的成绩永远能把球迷吸引到球场来。但你还得让食物好吃、设施到位、整个体验让人觉得花的钱值。

turns.en: And David, you're giving us a little bit of a peek into what it means to be the owner of a sports franchise, and I want to ask you a little bit more about that.
turns.zh: David，你让我们窥见了一点做体育球队老板意味着什么，我想再多问你一些这方面的东西。

turns.en: I think when people picture a sports owner, they picture somebody sitting in the box watching the game, or maybe close to the field watching the game, what surprised you the most about what the job actually entails, and how is this similar or different from running another business?
turns.zh: 我觉得人们想象一个体育老板的画面，往往是坐在包厢里看球，或者在球场边看比赛。这份工作实际包含的内容最让你意外的是什么？它跟经营其他生意有什么异同？

turns.en: Well, Carlisle owns lots of companies, and virtually nobody ever comes up to me on the street and says, hey, how's your company doing in the chemistry industry, or how many people are really employed by you in the aerospace industry, or how's your aerospace company doing?
turns.zh: 嗯，Carlyle 旗下有很多公司，但几乎没有任何人在街上拦住我说：嘿，你们化工行业的公司怎么样？你在航空航天行业雇了多少人？你的航空航天公司做得如何？

turns.en: This is a business where people come up to you all the time and talk about it. They want to know how a team is going, what are you going to do, how are you going to improve it, and so forth and so on.
turns.zh: 但棒球不一样——人们会不断来找你聊这个话题。他们想知道球队怎么样，你打算做什么，你打算怎么改进，等等等等。

turns.en: And the level of interest is a staggering. When you think about it, baseball teams, for example, are relatively modest revenue organizations, $200 million, $300 million, or something like that, and revenue annually.
turns.zh: 而且这种热情是惊人的。你想想看，棒球俱乐部其实是收入规模相对不大的组织，比如两三亿美元一年，大概那个量级。

turns.en: And that's modest compared to the kind of companies that Carlisle or other large firms like ours own. So it is something that people have a real pride in.
turns.zh: 跟 Carlyle 或者像我们这样的大型机构拥有的那些公司相比，这个规模算是小的。所以人们真的是对它有一种发自内心的自豪感。

turns.en: And it's a very interesting phenomenon. Why do people care about their local team? Why? They don't own it. If I do extremely well financially, they're not going to get any money out of it.
turns.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的现象。人们为什么在乎他们本地的球队？为什么？他们又不拥有它。如果我财务上做得非常成功，他们也不会因此分到一分钱。

turns.en: Why do they care? Because people want to feel that they have some attachment to success. People want to be successful. And if their local team is successful, they feel like they're successful.
turns.zh: 他们为什么在乎？因为人们想要那种跟成功有某种联系的感觉。人们想要成功。如果他们的本地球队成功了，他们就会觉得自己也成功了。

turns.en: Why do people root for their college team so much? Because they feel if the team does well, it makes them feel like their college is better and then they're better.
turns.zh: 人们为什么那么拼命地给自己的大学球队加油？因为他们觉得如果球队成绩好，就意味着自己的学校更好，进而自己也就更好。

turns.en: So people root for their local teams because they really want to say, I'm somebody important, my team is important, I'm successful, and I really am happy.
turns.zh: 所以人们为本地球队呐喊，是因为他们真的想说：我是重要的人，我的球队是重要的，我是成功的，我确实很快乐。

turns.en: Well, and I can attest to that here in New York City this summer. I know you spend a fair amount of time in New York, but when the New York Knicks won the NBA championship, I think you could definitely feel that in New York City.
turns.zh: 确实如此。今年夏天在纽约我就亲身感受到了。我知道你在纽约也花了不少时间，当 New York Knicks 拿下 NBA 总冠军的时候，你在纽约街头一定能感受到那种气氛。

turns.en: That feeling of success was shared by many millions of people across the five boroughs. There's no doubt. This weekend, I interviewed James Dolan in a panel and I asked them, what does it feel like to win a championship for 50 years compared to some of the criticism you've had before?
turns.zh: 那种成功感被五大区的数百万人共同分享了，毫无疑问。这个周末我在一个座谈会上采访了 James Dolan，我问他：赢下五十年来的第一个冠军是什么感觉，跟你之前承受的那些批评相比呢？

turns.en: And he obviously is very happy. So there's no doubt that fans really take enormous pride in their local team doing well, even though, as I mentioned, they don't own the team and if the team does well, they're not going to be putting money in their pocket necessarily.
turns.zh: 他显然非常开心。所以毫无疑问，球迷真的会因为本地球队表现出色而无比自豪——尽管正如我说的，他们又不拥有球队，球队好了他们也不一定口袋里多拿一分钱。

turns.en: So you mentioned James Dolan, who's another owner of a sports franchise. And I should have mentioned at the outset that part of the reason we're having this discussion is your new book, which is called Inside the Owner's Box, where you take us through what it means to own a professional sports franchise.
turns.zh: 你提到了 James Dolan，他也是一个体育球队的老板。我一开始就应该提到，我们做这期节目的部分原因是你的新书 Inside the Owner's Box，你在书里带我们走进了拥有一支职业球队到底意味着什么。

turns.en: And in there, you talk to other owners of other sports teams and you really talk about that owning a sports franchise is really an exercise in leadership.
turns.zh: 在书里你跟其他球队的老板对话，你真正讲的是：拥有一支球队其实是一场领导力的修炼。

turns.en: So I'm just curious, when you talk to some of these other sports owners, what were some of the common threads, the common things that you heard from them when you interviewed them?
turns.zh: 所以我很好奇，你跟这些其他体育老板交流的时候，有什么共同的主线？你在采访中听到他们共同说了些什么？

turns.en: They care more about winning than making money. Winning is everything. Making money, it's nice. You want to make money, you don't lose money, but they take much greater pride in the success on the field of all the owners I've talked to and I interviewed a number of them from different sports.
turns.zh: 他们在乎赢球胜过赚钱。赢就是一切。赚钱，挺好的——你想赚钱、不想亏钱，但在我交流过的所有老板里——我采访了好几位不同项目的老板——他们对赛场上的成功有着远远更大的自豪感。

turns.en: Nobody ever said to me, you know how much money I've made out of this or you know how we're doing so well financially, they all talked about what they had to do on the team to make the team better.
turns.zh: 从来没有人跟我说：你知道我从这支球队赚了多少吗，或者你知道我们财务上做得多好。他们都在谈他们需要做什么让球队变得更好。

turns.en: And that's owners take enormous pride. Also this weekend, I interviewed Bob Kraft, who's won six Super Bowls. And he never mentioned how much money the team has become worth as a result of.
turns.zh: 这就是老板们引以为傲的东西。也是这个周末，我采访了 Bob Kraft，他赢过六次超级碗（Super Bowl）。他一次都没有提球队因此升值了多少。

turns.en: He paid, I think, $172 million years ago. Now it's worth about eight or nine billion. He never mentioned that. It's something that owners, they know that the teams go up in value, but that's not their main focus.
turns.zh: 他大概多年前花了 1.72 亿美元买的球队，现在值大概八九十亿。但他从没提过这些。老板们知道球队在升值，但那不是他们的核心关注。

turns.en: It's winning, winning and being good to the community. Everybody wants to be good to the community that they represent and people want to win.
turns.zh: 核心就是赢、赢、对社区好。每个老板都想善待自己代表的社区，都想赢。

turns.en: Has that taken a little bit of an adjustment for you with the long history and finance of obviously focusing on making money, return on capital.
turns.zh: 对你来说，带着你在金融领域长期以来对盈利和资本回报的专注，做这种转变需要调整吗？

turns.en: And when you own a sports franchise, you still have that goal over the long term. But is it an adjustment to think about the timeframe a little bit different over which that return on investment pays off?
turns.zh: 当你拥有一支球队的时候，你当然长期还是会有那个目标。但换一种不同的时间框架来看待投资回报的兑现，对你来说是一种调整吗？

turns.en: Sure, it's much different in a typical private equity investment in five to seven years you're going to exit and you know that in advance and everybody knows that in advance.
turns.zh: 当然，这非常不同。一笔典型的私募股权投资，五到七年就要退出，你提前就知道，所有人都提前知道。

turns.en: In baseball or other professional sports, you have people owning these things sometimes for 10, 20, 30 years or more of these. Slime banners have owned it since 1972, the Yankees.
turns.zh: 但在棒球或其他职业体育里，人们持有球队可能一二十年、三十年甚至更久。Steinbrenner 家族从 1972 年起就拥有 Yankees 了。

turns.en: So you don't really look at it in quite that way. You also look at it as an investment, but you want to have some kind of discipline. You don't want to lose as much staggering sums of money, but you really want to make the team better.
turns.zh: 所以你不太用那种框架去看。你也会把它当投资来看，但你要有某种纪律性——你不想亏掉惊人的大笔金额——但你真正想做的是让球队变得更好。

turns.en: As we talk today, the Orioles have just signed a player from the New York Mets who was put on waivers, which means he's available to be purchased.
turns.zh: 就在我们聊天的今天，Orioles 刚从 New York Mets 签下一名被放入让渡名单（waivers）的球员，也就是说他可以被其他球队签走了。

turns.en: But doing so would cost a fair amount of money and we only have 30 games left in the season. But we thought it was worth it to spend that fair amount of money because we really want to win and get to the World Series and get to the championships and get to the playoffs if possible.
turns.zh: 但这样做要花不少钱，而且赛季只剩 30 场了。但我们觉得花那笔钱值得，因为我们真的很想赢，想打进世界系列赛（World Series），先争取进季后赛，去冲击总冠军。

turns.en: And these are things that you have to consider, not just the stadium and what's around the stadium, what's in the stadium, but also some of the day to day details around the players and the contracts and things like that.
turns.zh: 这些都是你必须考虑的事情——不只是球场和球场周围的建设、球场里的设施，还有球员、合同这些日常细节。

turns.en: In sports, you have two parts to it. You have the people that run the team, and it's generally overseen by somebody, might be called a head of baseball operations or a general manager, and they have somebody that oversees the business side, selling tickets, selling corporate suites, selling sponsorships, advertising, that kind of thing.
turns.zh: 体育运营分两个板块。一边是管球队的，通常由一个人来统筹，可能叫棒球运营总监或者总经理（general manager）。另一边是管商务的，负责卖门票、卖企业包厢、卖赞助、卖广告之类的。

turns.en: And so they're kind of separate. Very rarely do you see somebody in charge of both areas, though there are some people that do that. So generally, they both report to me and I have a co-owner, Mike Aragetti, who is the CEO of Aries.
turns.zh: 这两个板块基本是分开的。很少有人同时管两边，虽然也有个别例子。一般来说，两边都向我汇报。我有一位联合老板 Mike Arbit，他是 Orioles 的 CEO。

turns.en: We did this together. I'm the control partner because I'm a little bit older and I have more time to maybe do this, but he eventually will probably be the control owner, I hope so.
turns.zh: 这是我们一起做的。我是控股方，因为我年纪稍大一些、时间上更充裕来做这件事，但他将来很可能接棒成为控股老板，我希望如此。

turns.en: And so together, we kind of make these decisions and approve what goes on. But if you're overturning your baseball person or you're overturning your business person all the time, you probably should get somebody else.
turns.zh: 我们一起做这些决策，批准正在推进的事情。但如果你总是在推翻棒球运营那边的人，或者总是推翻商务那边的决定，那你可能该换人了。

turns.en: So generally, we know what they're doing. We consent to it unless we have some violent objection, which rarely happens. So today, they were letting me know about this player they wanted to get, and I thought made sense.
turns.zh: 所以我们大致知道他们在做什么。我们同意他们的方案，除非有强烈的反对意见，但那很少发生。今天他们告诉我他们想要签下那个球员，我觉得合理。

turns.en: So we went ahead with it. It sounds like you're setting strategic direction as an owner, but you hire a good team to help you in many facets of the business.
turns.zh: 所以我们就做了。听起来你作为老板定的是战略方向，然后招一个好的团队来帮你管理业务方方面面。

turns.en: That's the theory, but obviously there are owners like George Steinbrenner, who like to get in the middle of these things himself, recruit the players, sign the players, fire the players, do all the things he wanted.
turns.zh: 理论上是这样，但当然有些老板像 George Steinbrenner 那样，喜欢亲自插手——招球员、签球员、裁球员，什么他都自己来。

turns.en: He was a different character. We don't have owners quite like that today, but he made an incredible investment. He paid $8.8 million in 1972.
turns.zh: 他是那种完全不同的人物。今天的老板不太有像他那样的了，但他做了一笔不可思议的投资。1972 年他花了 880 万美元买的球队。

turns.en: He put in $250,000 in his own money. That's all he had to put in. And he syndicated the rest, and the team is now worth about $10 billion. You make the point in the book, David, that investing in sports franchises has become more popular.
turns.zh: 他自己只掏了 25 万美元，那就是他需要投入的全部。剩下的他做了银团分销（syndicated），现在球队价值大约 100 亿美元。David，你在书里提到了，体育投资已经变得更流行了。

turns.en: There's more teams, but also if you think about just media and television and the ability to watch sports globally, you talk about also sports gambling and the growth of that industry.
turns.zh: 球队数量更多了，但你只要想想媒体和电视、全球观看体育赛事的可能性，还有你谈到的体育博彩以及那个行业的增长。

turns.en: So this has certainly become an asset class, and passion investing is also becoming more common in today's markets. But what are some of the potential risks that you think investors underestimate when they enter the space?
turns.zh: 所以这确实已经成了一类资产，热情投资（passion investing）在今天的市场里也越来越普遍。但你认为投资者进入这个领域时会低估哪些潜在风险？

turns.en: Well, everything doesn't always go up to the sky forever. There's some times you have hiccups like we do in the business investing world. And so sports right now, I won't say it's a bubble, but clearly prices are going up, and it rates nobody anticipated.
turns.zh: 嗯，什么东西都不可能永远涨上天。总有时候会遇到波折，就像我们在投资行业里经常经历的那样。所以现在体育这块，我不说它是泡沫，但价格确实在上涨，而且上涨的幅度是没有人预料到的。

turns.en: Most recently we saw the Los Angeles Lakers were sold for $12.5 billion, one year if they sold for $10 billion, and that was just a few years after they were worth about $6 billion.
turns.zh: 最近我们看到 Los Angeles Lakers 以 125 亿美元被卖掉了，而几年前他们才 100 亿——那不过是球队估值大约 60 亿美元之后短短几年。

turns.en: The Boston Celtics just sold for $6.1 billion. They previously had been purchased for about $330 million. The Orioles came to Baltimore in 1954 for a purchase price of $2.2 million.
turns.zh: Boston Celtics 刚刚以 61 亿美元被卖掉了，之前大概花了 3.3 亿买的。Orioles 在 1954 年来到 Baltimore 的时候，收购价是 220 万美元。

turns.en: My partners and I paid $1.7 billion. So the prices have gone up, and a lot of people have made a lot of money. Some people have sold these teams after they own them for a few years.
turns.zh: 我和我的合伙人们付了 17 亿。所以价格一直在涨，很多人赚了很多钱。有些人持有几年之后就把球队卖掉了。

turns.en: Everything goes up forever, and therefore it's likely at some point there'll be a plateauing. But right now, people like it, and the reason they like it and the reason the values are going up, the TV contracts are fairly lucrative for the leagues.
turns.zh: 不可能什么东西永远上涨，所以到某个阶段肯定会趋于平稳。但现在人们喜欢这个市场，他们喜欢它、价值持续上升的原因之一是——电视转播合同对联盟来说非常丰厚。

turns.en: People are watching more sports than ever before, and they're more people. When I was growing up in Baltimore, the entire population of the United States might have been 170 million people.
turns.zh: 人们比以往任何时候看的体育都多，而且人也多了。我在 Baltimore 长大的时候，美国全国人口大概只有 1.7 亿。

turns.en: Now we're almost double that. Secondly, think about how many more teams there are. For example, when I was growing up in 1960, the number of NBA teams was eight.
turns.zh: 现在差不多翻了一倍。第二，你想想现在有多少球队。比如我 1960 年长大的时候，NBA 总共才 8 支球队。

turns.en: The number of NHL teams was six. That's it. The entire NHL was six teams. The entire NBA was eight teams. Now they have, I think, 30 or 32 teams.
turns.zh: NHL 只有 6 支，就这些。整个 NHL 只有 6 支球队。整个 NBA 只有 8 支。现在有 30 或 32 支了吧。

turns.en: So it's much different. You have more teams that you can support and root for, and there are more opportunities to invest as well. I think you had a fun statistic in the book about the number of minutes that Americans spend a year watching televised sports.
turns.zh: 所以完全不一样了。你有更多球队可以支持和呐喊，也有更多投资机会。我记得你在书里有个很有意思的数据，说美国人一年花多少分钟看体育转播。

turns.en: I think it was something like a trillion. It was a big number. Just staggering. And think about this. 100 most popular TV shows in any given year in the United States, 95 are live sports.
turns.zh: 我记得差不多是一万亿分钟，那个数字很大，简直惊人。你想想看——美国每年最热门的 100 个电视节目里，95 个是体育赛事直播。

turns.en: 95, the 100 most popular shows in any given year, at least certainly the last couple years, have been live sports. That's because people don't seem to be watching sitcoms anymore.
turns.zh: 95 个——最热门的 100 个节目里——至少近几年，都是体育直播。这是因为人们好像不再看情景喜剧了。

turns.en: They don't want to watch variety shows. They want live sports for whatever reason. And because people can now watch these live sports and sporting events almost anywhere or through streaming devices, it's an extremely popular way to entertain yourself.
turns.zh: 也不想看综艺节目。不知为什么就是想看体育直播。而现在人们几乎可以在任何地方通过流媒体设备看体育赛事，它已经成了一种极其主流的娱乐方式。

turns.en: When you were making the point before that nothing is linear. So there is volatility even in an asset class like investing in a sports franchise.
turns.zh: 你之前提到了没有什么是一路上涨的——即便是投资体育球队这样的资产类别也存在波动性。

turns.en: On the bid, we've spent a lot of time talking about the disruptive power of artificial intelligence, AI. And that's creating a lot of volatility in the markets in some cases in favor of some companies in some cases, not so much in favor of certain companies.
turns.zh: 在 The Bid 节目里我们花了很多时间讨论人工智能（AI）的颠覆力量。它在市场上制造了很多波动——有些公司因此受益，有些公司的处境就没那么好了。

turns.en: When you bought the Orioles back in March of 2024, this was the relatively early stages of AI. And I'm just curious, has AI changed your thinking about investing in sports at all?
turns.zh: 你 2024 年 3 月买下 Orioles 的时候，AI 还处于相对早期阶段。我很好奇，AI 有没有改变你对体育投资的看法？

turns.en: It hasn't changed my thinking about investing in sports, but AI is going to permeate our society and it will permeate sports. As you probably know, there was a discussion of how analytics were helping baseball many years ago.
turns.zh: AI 没有改变我对体育投资的看法，但 AI 将渗透到整个社会，也必将渗透到体育。你可能知道，很多年前就有了关于数据分析如何帮助棒球的讨论。

turns.en: A book was written called Moneyball and people all of a sudden realized you can use analytics to analyze baseball in ways that people didn't realize it wasn't just relying on your gut or experience.
turns.zh: 出了一本书叫 Moneyball，人们突然意识到可以用数据来分析棒球，而不再只是凭直觉或经验。

turns.en: Now, every team has detailed analytical staffs and now increasingly, these staffs are using AI. So increasingly, AI will be used and some will use it better than others.
turns.zh: 现在每支球队都有精细的数据分析团队，而且这些团队越来越多地在用 AI。所以 AI 的使用会越来越普遍，有些球队会比其他球队用得更好。

turns.en: But AI is going to be important for every part of society and certainly in sports. Certainly not only baseball, but sports in general, very data-driven business and helps you make better decisions.
turns.zh: AI 对社会每个领域都很重要，体育当然也不例外。不只是棒球，体育运动总体上都是非常数据驱动的行业，AI 能帮你做出更好的决策。

turns.en: As you're saying, AI could be just the supercharge to that decision making. Correct. It's clearly going to change the way some analytics are done.
turns.zh: 正如你所说，AI 可能就是给决策过程的一管燃料。没错。它显然会改变一些数据分析的做法。

turns.en: But again, AI is not yet permeated baseball completely and it's going to take a while before it does, but it's obviously here now. David, if the last 20 years were about sports becoming an institutional asset class, what do you think defines the next 20 years and where do you see some of the biggest opportunities?
turns.zh: 但话说回来，AI 还没有完全渗透到棒球里，要彻底渗透还需要一段时间，不过它显然已经来了。David，如果过去 20 年是体育成为机构化资产类别的 20 年，你觉得未来 20 年什么会定义这个行业？你看到哪些最大的机会？

turns.en: Well, in the sports world, let me just say that there are a lot of wealthy people buying sports teams, but there are a lot of people who are smaller investors who say, I want to be in there too, but I don't have a billion dollars.
turns.zh: 嗯，在体育界，这么说吧，有很多富豪在买球队，但也有一些资金规模小一些的投资者说：我也想进来，但我没有 10 亿美元。

turns.en: They're investing in partnerships that will aggregate a lot of investors that might be at, I don't know, $100,000, $200,000, $500,000 level.
turns.zh: 他们会去投那种集合基金（partnership），汇集很多中小投资者——可能是 10 万、20 万、50 万美元那个量级的。

turns.en: They can buy into a sports partnership. That sports partnership will buy a team and the person could say, I'm a part owner of that team or so forth.
turns.zh: 他们可以通过体育投资合伙企业入股。这个合伙企业去买一支球队，然后那个人就可以说：我是这支球队的部分股东了。

turns.en: Clearly that is going forward. In terms of non-sports related things, nothing is going to rival artificial intelligence for some time. But overall, if I were to say the next five or 10 years, areas that I think would be very important are things like quantum computing, fusion will no doubt be a big thing in the future as well, and probably things related to biotech, CRISPR and other kinds of vaccines
turns.zh: 这是明确的方向。至于非体育的领域，在相当长一段时间里没有什么能跟人工智能相提并论。但总的说来，如果让我说未来五到十年非常重要的领域，我觉得是量子计算（quantum computing）、核聚变（fusion）无疑也会是一个大方向，还有生物科技（biotech）、CRISPR 和其他类型的疫苗

turns.en: will no doubt be an important part of the investing world. And actually, this helps me with the follow-up question because when you think about passion investing and you think about diversifying your portfolio, not everybody can buy a sports team.
turns.zh: 无疑也会是投资领域非常重要的一部分。实际上这些也帮了我的忙，因为我想接着问：当你想到热情投资、想到分散投资组合，不是每个人都能买一支球队。

turns.en: That is certainly reserved for a select few, but there are other sectors and themes that maybe people can be considering for some of their longer-term investments.
turns.zh: 那肯定是少数人的特权，但还有其他行业和主题，也许人们可以在长期投资里考虑。

turns.en: I think you started to touch on those, but maybe talk a little bit more about what you mean there. The world is always looking for new opportunities.
turns.zh: 我觉得你已经开始提到那些了，能不能再具体讲讲？世界总是在寻找新的机会。

turns.en: In the investment world, people always want to be in the ground floor of something. What is going to be in the ground floor? If I take an example of something I just mentioned, which is quantum computing.
turns.zh: 在投资界，人们总想抓住某个领域的第一波机会。什么是下一个起点？就拿我刚提到的一个例子来说——量子计算。

turns.en: Quantum computing has always been said to be five years from now. In other words, every year, people say it's another five years. But now, I think we are really getting close to having quantum computing.
turns.zh: 量子计算一直被称为'还有五年'，也就是说每年人们都说还要再等五年。但现在我觉得我们真的要接近量子计算的落地了。

turns.en: There's good opportunities there to invest or our publicly traded companies that are quantum companies. That will revolutionize the computer industry because it can go make decisions much more rapidly than current computers.
turns.zh: 那里面有好的投资机会，也有一些上市公司是做量子的。它将彻底改变计算机行业，因为它的决策速度会远远超过现有计算机。

turns.en: That will be a gigantic area in the future. I think people can invest in that and we'll be able to take a biotech revolution. I'm on the board of Moderna.
turns.zh: 未来那会是一个巨大的领域。我觉得人们可以投这个方向，我们也即将迎来一场生物科技革命。我在 Moderna 的董事会。

turns.en: Moderna is a company that had a technology that didn't get a lot of raves for a while, but then when it developed the COVID vaccine, people began to realize that this RNA technology can really do something wonderful.
turns.zh: Moderna 这家公司有一项技术，之前很长时间不太受关注，但后来它研发出新冠疫苗，人们才意识到 mRNA 技术真的能做出了不起的事情。

turns.en: It's just been announced that they have trials coming through that have been very successful in melanoma cancer for a vaccine. There's also been news recently that a vaccine in effect for pancreatic cancer has proven to be successful and has been approved by the FDA.
turns.zh: 最近刚宣布他们在黑色素瘤癌症疫苗方面的临床试验非常成功。最近还有新闻说一种针对胰腺癌的疫苗也被证明有效，已经获得了 FDA 批准。

turns.en: All kinds of medical revolutions will be in front of us. Then I should mention space. The biggest IPO ever in the United States is SpaceX. It has a staggering valuation, but that has made other people say that their space company should be taken public.
turns.zh: 各种医学革命都将在我们面前展开。然后我还得提太空。美国有史以来最大的 IPO 是 SpaceX，估值高得惊人。但它让其他人也开始说，他们的太空公司也该上市了。

turns.en: There are going to be a lot of space-related companies that are going to be going public or being created in the next couple of years. Another area that's really attractive is one that people shied away from before, but it's called aerospace defense.
turns.zh: 未来几年会有很多太空相关的公司上市或成立。另一个真正有吸引力的领域，之前人们有些回避，就是航空航天防御（aerospace defense）。

turns.en: As we've seen, drone technology is changing the way we fight wars for better or worse. As a result, more and more people are going to invest in aerospace defense, particularly countries and companies in countries that are not yet now possessing a major aerospace defense complex.
turns.zh: 我们已经看到了，无人机技术正在改变战争的方式，不管这是好事还是坏事。结果是，越来越多的人会投资航空航天防御领域，特别是在那些目前还没有大型航空航天防御体系的国家。

turns.en: That's a lot of countries. David, I think you've been listening to some of our episodes of the bid because some of these are topics that we've touched on with some of the investors here at BlackRock.
turns.zh: 那可是很多国家。David，我想你一直在听我们的 The Bid 节目，因为其中一些话题我们在 BlackRock 这边跟一些投资人也聊到过。

turns.en: It's good to hear that you also share some of the positive views on some of these longer-term themes. I do. David, you said you grew up in Baltimore.
turns.zh: 很高兴你也对这些长期主题抱有相似的乐观态度。确实如此。David，你说你是在 Baltimore 长大的。

turns.en: Do you remember the first time you went to an Orioles game? Sure. My father took me to an Orioles game when I was probably seven or eight, and I didn't really know what I was doing.
turns.zh: 你还记得第一次看 Orioles 比赛是什么时候吗？当然记得。大概七八岁的时候我父亲带我去看了 Orioles 的比赛，那时候我其实什么也不懂。

turns.en: I rooted for the team. I remember the food was good, the hot dog tasted great. It's amazing how hot dogs taste better in a baseball stadium than tastes at home.
turns.zh: 我就跟着给球队加油。我记得吃的特别好，热狗特别香。奇怪的是，球场里的热狗就是比家里的好吃。

turns.en: Just everybody cheering for the team and idolizing players. I used to go try to get the autographs to the players when I was eight or nine years old, and I don't know what I did with those autographs.
turns.zh: 周围所有人都在给球队呐喊、崇拜那些球员。我八九岁的时候会跑去要球员签名，但后来那些签名我都不知道放哪儿了。

turns.en: I wish I had them because they're probably worth a lot more now, but people come to me for autographs and the players, but I keep saying, I'm an owner.
turns.zh: 真希望那些签名还在，因为现在它们肯定更值钱了。不过现在人们来找我要签名——就像找球员要一样——但我老说：我是老板啊。

turns.en: You don't want my autograph, but rather than explain to somebody why I have an autograph, that's not worth anything. I just sign it, but I'm not really good at signing a baseball because it's curved.
turns.zh: 我的签名不值钱的。不过跟别人解释这个又太麻烦了，所以我还是签。但我其实不太擅长在棒球上签名，因为它是弧形的。

turns.en: I have to print it out. I'm guessing when you were at those games, you probably had aspirations of being a player for the team, but maybe not the owner of the team.
turns.zh: 我猜你小时候看那些比赛的时候，大概梦想过当球队的球员，但应该没想到过有一天会拥有这支球队吧。

turns.en: Well, when I was a little boy, I was a good little leaguer at the age of seven, and then around eight or nine I peaked. I was an all-star, but it was a Jewish little league, and so everybody's not going to be Sandy Kofak.
turns.zh: 嗯，我小时候大概七岁的时候打少棒（Little League）打得还不错，然后差不多八九岁就巅峰了。我入选了全明星，但那是个犹太人少棒联盟，所以不是每个人都能成为 Sandy Koufax 的。

turns.en: So, no, I probably realized my athletic potential was probably over at a 10 or 11. You've done well for yourself, especially as a, not only a private equity investor, but also following that sports passion that you have.
turns.zh: 所以没有，大概十岁十一岁的时候我就知道自己在运动方面没什么前途了。你真的很成功——不仅是作为一个私募股权投资者，还追随了你对体育的那份热情。

turns.en: David, people who know you know that you also have an affinity for American history, and there's nothing more central to American history than the sport of baseball.
turns.zh: David，了解你的人都知道你对美国历史有一种特别的热爱，而没有什么比棒球更能代表美国的历史了。

turns.en: Thanks for giving us a behind-the-scenes peek of what it means to own a baseball team, a sports franchise, the lessons and leadership that we can take from that, and thank you for doing it here on The Bid.
turns.zh: 感谢你让我们看到了幕后——拥有一支棒球队、一支体育球队意味着什么，我们能从中收获的领导力和经验教训，也感谢你来到 The Bid 跟我们分享这些。

turns.en: My pleasure. Thank you for having me. Thanks for listening to this episode of The Bid. If you enjoy the show and want to support the podcast, consider telling your friends about us or sharing an episode that really resonated with you.
turns.zh: 我的荣幸，谢谢邀请。感谢收听这一期的 The Bid。如果你喜欢这个节目、想支持我们，可以把我们推荐给朋友，或者分享一期真正引起你共鸣的节目。

turns.en: Next up, I'm speaking with Reed Mengi about space, the final investing frontier. Make sure to subscribe to The Bid so you won't miss the episode.
turns.zh: 下一期，我将和 Reed Mengi 聊太空——投资的最后一片前沿。记得订阅 The Bid，不错过每一期。
